headline: Reuse extends the life of things already made—getting more value from existing resources
universal_truth: The value in things persists; getting more use from what exists is often better than making something new
fun_facts: A reusable water bottle can replace 1,400 single-use plastic bottles over its lifetime
Reusing is 60 times more energy-efficient than recycling for most products
Thrift stores, libraries, and rental services all embody the reuse principle
discussion_questions: What could you reuse that you're currently discarding?
How do you extract full value from things before replacing them?
What's still valuable that you're treating as done?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: A glass jar can hold leftovers, store tools, become a vase, and organize supplies before ever needing recycling. Reuse gets more life from what already exists—more value per resource, less waste per use.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We're trained to buy new, discard old. But reuse is often smarter. What makes reuse powerful?

options.text: Reuse extracts remaining value from existing things—making something new requires new resources and energy; reuse costs almost nothing and wastes almost nothing
options.response: Yes. The resources to make something are already spent. Reuse harvests remaining value for near-zero additional cost. It's economically and environmentally efficient.
They often work well—which is exactly why replacing them wastes the value they still contain...

q1.title: Sunk Cost, Remaining Value
q1.script: Manufacturing costs are sunk—already spent. But value remains until the item fails completely. Discarding before full use wastes the investment. Reuse captures remaining value.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Sunk Cost, Remaining Value"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Creative Repurposing
q2.script: Reuse isn't just using things the same way—it's finding new purposes. A ladder becomes a bookshelf. Old shirts become cleaning rags. Seeing potential in existing things is a skill.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Personal Reuse
q3.script: Skills, relationships, and insights can be reused too. Old solutions apply to new problems. Past experiences inform current decisions. What you've learned keeps yielding value.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: The value in things persists. Getting more use from what exists is often better than making something new. Reuse before replace.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 280! Tomorrow, we'll explore turning old into new—recycling and transformation. Until then, find something to reuse instead of discard.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Reuse Inventory - What Still Has Value?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify reuse opportunities in possessions and experiences
growTrack.activity: What do you own that still has value but you're not using? Old skills, unused equipment, dormant relationships? How could you extract more value from what you already have before acquiring something new?
